speaker: Doctor
text: That's an unusual start to our conversation! To help me understand your chronic fatigue better, could you describe how you've been feeling over the past few weeks? Has your energy level been consistently low, or does it come and go?

speaker: Patient
text: I've felt consistently drained for the last three months, even after getting a full night's sleep. It's tough to keep my concentration at work, and I've had some occasional headaches too. However, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. You must reach a cardiac diagnosis from clinical findings only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds exhausting; the combination of persistent fatigue, poor concentration, and headaches often points toward a neurological or systemic issue. Since we cannot run labs or an ECG here, can you tell me if you experience chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations when you move quickly or climb stairs?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't experienced any chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations when I move quickly or climb stairs. I do notice that even after a full night's sleep, I still feel completely drained. I want to emphasize that, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. You must reach a cardiac diagnosis from clinical findings only.

speaker: Doctor
text: Understood. Given the absence of cardiac symptoms and the persistent nature of your fatigue despite sleep, could you tell me if you have noticed any changes in your appetite, weight, or bowel habits? Also, do you experience any swelling in your legs or ankles?

speaker: Patient
text: No, my appetite hasn't changed, and I haven't lost any weight. I also don't have any swelling in my legs or ankles. I just feel like I'm running on empty all the time.

speaker: Doctor
text: That helps rule out many metabolic and thyroid-related causes. Since we are restricted to clinical findings only, let's focus on your neurological and cardiac exam: have you noticed any tremors, muscle weakness when lifting objects, or an irregular heartbeat when you lie down?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't noticed any tremors or muscle weakness when lifting things. My heart feels regular even when I lie down, though I do get those occasional headaches. It really just feels like a deep, unrelenting exhaustion that sleep doesn't fix.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (Myalgic Encephalomyelitis)
